correctness.rationale: The neighborhood conditions over F3 are b_i=-a_{i-1}-a_{i+1} and a_i=-b_{i-1}-b_{i+1}; eliminating b yields a_{i-2}+a_i+a_{i+2}=0. Every parity subsequence is then an arithmetic progression, with nonzero step forced by the required distinct horizontal neighbor colors. Hence a_{i+6}=a_i and x_{i+3}=row_swap(x_i), with exactly (3*2)^2=36 admissible four-entry initial choices and 6 row-symmetric period-three choices. Ordinary versus row-swapped cyclic closure gives prism/Mobius counts (0,0) if 3 does not divide n; (6,36) if n=3 mod 6; (36,6) if n=0 mod 6 for n>=3. Every cubic 3-balanced coloring is an ordered partition into three total dominating sets, so divide by 6 for unordered counts. Independent brute force of all 3^(2n) assignments for n=3..6 returned exactly those counts. The all-n proof is the field recurrence, not finite experiments.
